stories.summary: Singapore's Home Affairs Ministry said Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, left Singapore in February and has been barred from re-entering after an investigation into possible offences linked to servers bought and exported via Singapore to Malaysia. Police found insufficient evidence of offences and said the probe did not concern espionage; investigations into Megaspeed and six individuals continue.
stories.title: Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entry after Megaspeed investigation
stories.why: Singapore is at the centre of the chip-diversion allegations behind Nvidia's leadership crisis — and has now stated its own findings publicly.

stories.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB warned customers against letting third-party AI agents access their bank accounts, citing scam risks and unclear liability if something goes wrong. The banks said they had not yet seen customers using such agents, but urged people to use only the banks' own AI tools.
stories.title: Singapore banks warn against third-party AI agents as liability risk flagged
stories.why: Agentic AI is reaching personal banking before the liability rules are settled — Singapore's big three banks are drawing the line early.

stories.summary: A World Weather Attribution study published on 13 November found human-induced climate change added about 1.6°C of heat to Indonesia's August–October fire season, while a very strong El Niño halved rainfall. The fires razed nearly 2.9 million hectares and caused more than 400,000 respiratory infections in Indonesia; Singapore hospitals saw 20% more emergency visits for haze-related conditions.
stories.title: Climate change and El Niño worsened Indonesia haze, study finds
stories.why: The haze that choked the region this year was made measurably worse by warming — and the study says such seasons are increasingly predictable and preventable.

stories.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect, ending his 33-year leadership of the AI chipmaker after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US authorities suspect of links to Chinese intelligence. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey Jones becomes the company's first chairman; Nvidia shares fell more than 4%.
stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
stories.why: The world's most valuable chipmaker has lost the CEO who built it, days before its quarterly earnings — with national-security questions still open.

stories.summary: A global Microsoft outage hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot, with Downdetector logging more than 131,000 Outlook reports in the US and hundreds in Singapore. Microsoft blamed elevated load that made some servers unavailable and said it had restarted them; services began recovering during the morning.
stories.title: Microsoft outage hits Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide
stories.why: A single cloud failure took down the work tools of millions on a Friday morning — a reminder of how concentrated workplace software has become.

stories.summary: Two US nonprofits sued Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and xAI in a San Francisco court, arguing that AI development is uncontrollable and poses a risk to humanity. They are asking the court to halt further AI development and order the deletion of copies of advanced models.
stories.title: US nonprofits sue tech giants to halt AI development
stories.why: The lawsuit is a long shot, but it puts the 'pause AI' argument before a court for the first time — against every major lab at once.

stories.summary: US stocks fell on Thursday as investors weighed Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation and renewed uncertainty over the Iran war. The Nasdaq fell 0.39% to 25,366.09 and the S&P 500 0.35%, while Nvidia shares dropped more than 4% to a 52-week low. Oil rose sharply, with Brent up 3.3% to US$95.82 a barrel, and Australian shares were set to open 0.7% lower.
stories.title: US stocks fall as Nvidia shake-up weighs on Wall Street
stories.why: One resignation knocked the world's biggest chipmaker and dragged the whole AI trade down with it — and lifted oil at the same time.

stories.summary: Anthropic's initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, Bloomberg reported, in what could be the largest first-time share sale ever. The Claude maker is selling 825 million shares at US$70–78 each to raise up to US$64.4 billion, alongside a US$26 billion private placement, valuing it at up to US$1.4 trillion fully diluted. Pricing is set for 18 November, with trading from 19 November.
stories.title: Anthropic IPO about six times oversubscribed, Bloomberg reports
stories.why: Demand for the biggest IPO in history is running far ahead of supply — a fresh test of whether the AI boom still has room to run.

stories.summary: Standard Chartered's third-quarter profit jumped 46%, with chief executive Bill Winters saying geopolitical fragmentation is an advantage for the bank. Wealth Solutions income rose 26% to US$1.1 billion and Global Markets income rose 20%.
stories.title: Standard Chartered profit jumps 46% as CEO bets on a fragmenting global economy
stories.why: A bank built for cross-border Asia is turning fragmentation into profit — the opposite of the usual globalisation story.

stories.summary: The US Navy has quietly fired or removed several senior officers without its usual public announcements, drawing pushback from Congress. Two Democratic lawmakers said the Navy failed to inform Congress that it fired the entire leadership of the nuclear-powered attack submarine USS South Dakota after an underwater collision, and that a destroyer commander deployed to the Middle East was relieved in September. The dispute looms over acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao's confirmation hearing next week.
stories.title: US Navy quietly fired commanders, drawing congressional pushback
stories.why: A submarine grounding kept from Congress for a month raises questions about Navy transparency — just as its top civilian faces confirmation.

stories.summary: France's Ministry of Armed Forces announced a new AI defence resilience centre in Rennes, aiming for NATO recognition within the NATO Centres of Excellence framework. The centre will work with partner nations on the resilience of military AI systems.
stories.title: France to spearhead new AI defence resilience centre with partner nations
stories.why: AI is now a defence-resilience problem, not just a capability race — and France wants the NATO-recognised hub for it.

stories.summary: Germany and Poland will use SATIM's AI to analyse synthetic-aperture radar satellite imagery, building on SATIM's cooperation with Rheinmetall for the German armed forces and supporting Poland's MikroSAR programme.
stories.title: Germany, Poland tap SATIM to analyse military satellite imagery
stories.why: Two NATO allies are pooling AI analysis of radar satellite imagery — a quiet but telling step in European defence integration.

stories.summary: Russian propaganda exploited the detention of SBU Major General Serhii Duka in Ukraine's Operation 'Carthage' to push narratives about corruption, internal divisions and a weakening Ukrainian government, and to question Western oversight of aid, according to Ukrainian National News.
stories.title: Russian propaganda exploits Ukrainian anti-corruption detention to push division narratives
stories.why: A real anti-corruption case is being repurposed as a propaganda asset — the classic pattern of exploiting a genuine event to erode trust in Kyiv.

tldr: Singapore bars Alice Huang from re-entry after the Megaspeed probe, as the Nvidia scandal reaches home.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years; CFO Colette Kress takes over as interim chief.
US stocks fall as Nvidia's resignation rattles Wall Street, with oil up sharply on Iran uncertainty.
The US Navy quietly fired senior officers, including a submarine command triad, drawing Congress's ire.
Russian propaganda is exploiting a Ukrainian anti-corruption detention to push division narratives.
